document: closing procedure for the two remaining goal items
purpose: Written in advance so the steps are deterministic rather than improvised when the profile ends. The ledger already states the exact condition for item 5, and this makes the rest explicit.

item5_stress24h.currentlyMissing: zero such files, which is correct while the profile is still running
item5_stress24h.decisionRule: The ledger already says it stays NOT_RUN until a 24h run reports passed=true with durationMet=true. That is the rule: read the report rather than infer, and set PASS only if both fields are true.
item5_stress24h.ifPassed: Set the entry to PASS, fill finishedUtc, and record observedSeconds, requestedSeconds, completedChunks, refills and peak heap from the report.
item5_stress24h.ifFailed: Leave it NOT_RUN and record the failure verbatim, including the failure field. Nothing is smoothed over.
item5_stress24h.eitherWay: Copy stress-report.json into docs/evidence/ before anything else touches build/, because a later build or clean removes it.

item2_gameTest.independentCheck: Compare that count against the inventory recorded before the run: 129 methods across 34 classes. The two figures come from different sources, so agreement is a check rather than a restatement.
item2_gameTest.evidence: build/reports/gametest/results.xml, which is rebuilt each run - copy it to docs/evidence/ as well.
item2_gameTest.budget: About 3.65 hours, with no gradle timeout and an 8 GB default heap.

stepsNotToForget: Test-S5Release.ps1 afterwards: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/Test-S5Release.ps1 -TestRoot build\run\s5release
Update the six-item table in the report with the item 2 and item 5 results
Refresh docs/evidence/INDEX-20261007.json once no further files will be added
Distinguish clearly what automation proved from the nine real-machine items, which do not change

s5ReleaseExpectation.expectedOutcome: The script will throw, because verifyReleaseArtifacts throws on the version string and the script treats a non-zero exit as failure.
s5ReleaseExpectation.thisIsCorrect: The gate is refusing to sign a preview. The ledger already records this under version-lock and full-package.
s5ReleaseExpectation.readThisInsteadOfExitStatus: execution.json in the evidence directory: remapJarShaMatch is the reproducibility answer, and passed false is the version gate.
s5ReleaseExpectation.stillWorthRunning: Yes. Both builds run with the offline and strict flags, which re-exercises the offline path at current source and dates that item, and the SHA comparison is a genuine reproducibility result.

verifyBeforeRunningS5Release: Confirm the step 2 and 3 copies are present in docs/evidence/. If they are not, stop: that script's clean removes build/run/serverSmoke/vanilla/<runId>/ and build/s5-stress-24h2.log, and nothing else will regenerate them.

gameTestVerificationTargets.whyBothFigures: The two differ by the arch-preparation pair, which ran on 10-03 under old names but whose bodies were rewritten in b90f5fc to inject failure through the durable plan reader instead of plan-schema construction. So 21 have never run under any name, and 23 have never run in the form they now have.
gameTestVerificationTargets.crossCheckAfterTheRun: Count testcase entries in build/reports/gametest/results.xml and require 129, then confirm all six classes appear. WallArchPreparationGameTests should contribute exactly four cases; anything fewer means its re-bodied pair or the new case was skipped.
gameTestVerificationTargets.theRenameHistory: Verified across all eight gametest commits since the 10-03 run: seven are pure additions and only b90f5fc removed anything, so no other class hides a rename.

stepCountNote: Seven steps. The archive step was inserted as step 4 after the JUnit results were overwritten during the session.

theTwentyThreeNamesToConfirm.note: Post-run verification should confirm these appear in results.xml, not just that the total is 129. A count alone cannot show a class was skipped while another gained cases.

roundBudgetConstraint.superseded: The earlier figures here assumed a round took 1.6 to 2.6 minutes, which made the profile look as though it would outlast the round budget. That assumption is gone.
roundBudgetConstraint.whatChanged: The user asked for progress checks every 30 minutes rather than every few rounds, and pointed out that goal rounds are issued immediately on completion, so spacing checks by round count cannot produce a 30-minute interval. Each round now waits to the next 30-minute mark before reporting, which makes a round about 30 minutes.
therefore: The profile will finish well inside the round budget, so no raise to maxGoalRounds is needed.
The earlier advice to keep each round to one action still holds, but for a different reason - it keeps reporting readable, not because rounds are scarce.
Post-profile steps can still be batched into single rounds: runGameTest and the JUnit test task take hours, and Test-S5Release takes about a minute for two builds.
roundBudgetConstraint.theEarlierShapeStillFits: Round A starts gradlew test runGameTest as a background job. Round B collects it and archives both result sets. Round C runs Test-S5Release and writes the closing summary.

exactCommands.step2CopyEvidence: Copy stress-report.json, the samples directory and header.json from build/run/serverSmoke/vanilla/s5stress24h20261007084723/build/stress-reports/run-1791334079847/ into docs/evidence/, plus build/s5-stress-24h2.log
exactCommands.step3GameTest: gradlew runGameTest --no-daemon --console=plain, then copy build/reports/gametest/results.xml into docs/evidence/
exactCommands.step5StressVerdict: Do NOT run tools/Test-S5Stress.ps1 here. It is a launcher, not a verifier: it starts gradlew runS5Stress with -Hours defaulting to 24 and blocks until that profile ends, so using it at closing time would begin a second 24-hour run and contend with the first. Instead read the report the finished profile wrote, at build/run/serverSmoke/vanilla/s5stress24h20261007084723/build/stress-reports/run-*/stress-report.json, and judge it by the same rule the script uses: passed requires passed==true and durationMet==true in that report, since the fixture halts with server.halt(false) and therefore exits 0 even when the profile failed.
exactCommands.warningAboutStep5: If Test-S5Stress.ps1 is ever run deliberately, its TestRoot must include serverSmoke\vanilla and must sit under build\run; a path like build\run\s5stress24h... passes the guard but holds no stress-reports directory, which yields a fail-closed passed=false that looks like a profile failure.
exactCommands.warningAboutStep4: Test-S5Release throws by design because the version gate fails; read execution.json for remapJarShaMatch rather than the exit status.

step3ExactCommand.whyTestIsIncluded: They are independent tasks; runGameTest writes only build/reports/gametest/results.xml, and step 4 archives build/test-results/test which only test produces.
step3ExactCommand.heapNote: Do not pass -PgreatwallTestHeap unless needed. build.gradle only adds -Xmx when that property is set, otherwise the gameTest JVM uses the JVM default, which on this 31.9 GB machine is about 8 GB. Note that gradle.properties sets org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx2G for the Gradle daemon, which is a different JVM and does not bound the test run.
step3ExactCommand.resultsPath: build/reports/gametest/results.xml, from the vmArg -Dfabric-api.gametest.report-file=../../reports/gametest/results.xml relative to the run directory.
step3ExactCommand.whyVerifyByName: A pass message reports a total, and a total cannot show that one class was skipped while another gained cases. The script reads the expected names from the source and reports missing and unexpected entries, exiting non-zero unless the sets match.

orderedSteps: 1. Confirm the profile ended, and confirm it by a test rather than by reading the time. stress-report.json appearing under the run's stress-reports directory is the signal, but the decisive check is that build/s5-stress-24h2.log can be opened exclusively - the running profile holds it locked, so a successful exclusive open proves the writer is gone. Copying the log while it is still locked fails, and this is the step where that would be discovered.

2. Copy into docs/evidence/: stress-report.json, the whole samples directory, header.json, and build/s5-stress-24h2.log. Two further items under build/ also have no durable copy and are destroyed by step 5's clean: build/s5-stress-1h-evidence/stress-report-passed.json, the only record of the 1-hour profile, and build/smoke-pass.log. The 1-hour report has been archived to docs/evidence/s5/s5-stress-1h-20261007/stress-report.json. The smoke log is 17.68 GB and cannot be copied; its decisive lines are already transcribed verbatim into docs/evidence/s1c/real-wall-traversal-pass-20261007.json and were verified character for character, so losing it costs no evidence.

3. Run gradlew test runGameTest. Both are needed: they are independent tasks, and runGameTest writes only build/reports/gametest/results.xml while the JUnit results in build/test-results/test come from test alone. Verified with a dry run - the test task's dependency graph does not include runGameTest. Then copy build/reports/gametest/results.xml into docs/evidence/.

4. Before anything else touches the build directory, copy the whole of build/test-results/test into docs/evidence/ as a dated archive. Gradle's test task clears and rewrites that directory, so any later filtered run - a spot check of one or two classes - destroys the full set. This step exists because that happened on 2026-10-07: two filtered runs replaced 103 XML files covering 629 tests with a single file covering 2, and no archived copy was complete enough to restore them.
5. Only now run Test-S5Release.ps1 - its first gradle argument is clean, twice, which deletes build/ entirely
6. Read execution.json rather than the exit status, since the version gate makes it throw

7. Update the six-item table, the acceptance ledger and the evidence index. When updating the ledger, also repoint the stress-24h entry's log field: it currently reads build/s5-stress-24h2.log, which step 5's clean deletes, so leaving it would create a dead reference. Point it at the copy made in step 2. The top-level evidenceNote calls the log fields live locations that regenerate each run, which is true for the JUnit and gametest paths but not for the stress log - that one does not regenerate and must be archived.
